# `Q-1-22` — Unrecognized Tag

> A YAML tag is not one of the tags Quarto knows how to interpret.

## What this means

Quarto reserves a small family of YAML tags for controlling merge
behavior and value interpretation. This error fires when a value
carries a tag Quarto does not recognize as one of those — usually
a custom tag from another tool or a tag that does not match the
shape Quarto's tag parser expects.

Recognized tags combine merge operations and interpretation hints:
`!prefer`, `!concat`, `!md`, `!str`, `!path`, `!glob`, `!expr`,
and underscore-joined combinations such as `!prefer_md`.

## Why this happens

The two typical situations:

- **A tag from a different tool** has appeared in Quarto's
  configuration. Custom tags from a data-processing pipeline, for
  instance, may carry through into a configuration file by accident.
- **A tag that looks like a Quarto tag but is not.** A misspelled
  recognized tag — different from `Q-1-21`, which warns about an
  unknown *component* inside an otherwise well-formed tag — may
  surface here when the parser cannot fit it into the expected
  shape at all.

## How to fix

Remove the tag if the value does not need it. The value will be
treated as an ordinary YAML scalar.

If you intended a Quarto tag, check that you used one of the
recognized names listed above. Quarto's tag parser is strict about
the components it accepts.

## Related

- [`Q-1-21`](Q-1-21.qmd) — unknown tag component: an *otherwise valid* tag
  contains a component name Quarto does not recognize.
- [`Q-1-26`](Q-1-26.qmd) — invalid tag character: the tag contains characters
  outside the allowed set.
